brief.headline: They're a pure trader (100.0% traded revenue) — push them to the maker's price and line up a direct-from-manufacturer backup.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price cut to match what the manufacturer charges, before their reseller margin.
priceAsk.target: Target the lower end of the typical market band — ₹0.65–0.80/pc for caps — at our volume; their 100.0% traded revenue means every rupee we pay includes a margin they add on top of the maker's price.
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume. Since they make nothing themselves (0.0% manufactured), their price is the maker's cost plus their cut — so we benchmark to the maker.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Ask them to match the 105 days they already take to pay their own suppliers — we stay at 30 days.

brief.financialLeverage: They're weak — a money-health score of 2/10 and in the grey zone (Altman Z-score 1.58) — so they need our ₹65.27 L badly (1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue). They keep just 2.8% of every ₹100 they sell, so a big price squeeze could tip them over. The smart play: push hard on the trader's margin (their price vs the maker's), not on squeezing their thin 2.8% kept profit, and line up a direct manufacturer as a second source to reduce our risk. They already take 105 days to pay their own suppliers (vs 57 days for similar firms), so they can't credibly ask us for faster payment.

evidence.point: They make nothing — every item is resold, so their price includes a middleman margin
We are 1.19% of everything they sell — real leverage
evidence.figure: Our ₹65.27 L vs their ₹54.69 Cr revenue

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — makes pharma bottles and caps directly, a strong second-source to cut out the middleman.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-packaging leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) — makes containers and closures for pharma, robust and profitable.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (market backup)
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — manufacturer of rigid plastic materials, pan-India presence.

risks: Their 2/10 money-health score and grey-zone distress (1.58) mean supply could wobble — don't put more than 50% of this item through them until a second source is live.
Pending legal case(s) flagged in their filings — ask what the case is about and whether it affects production or delivery.
They operate on 2.8% kept profit — if we push price too hard and they can't pass it back to their supplier, they may walk or cut corners on quality.
100.0% traded revenue means they have no control over the maker's lead time or quality — if the upstream supplier fails, so do they.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to work directly with the manufacturer to get the maker's price — can you introduce us, or match that price yourself to keep the business?
